construction_markdown:
No new leaderboard code is submitted. Two spectral-amplification architectures are resolved.

First, let `F=F_2[θ]/(θ^16+θ^5+θ^3+θ^2+1)`, `A=span_F2{1,θ,…,θ^14}`, and let `R⊂F^A` be evaluation of `F[X]_{≤64}`. Each `z=Σz_iθ^i` is encoded by the affine block `Φ(z)_y=z_0+Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`, `y∈F_2^15`. The resulting shared RS–RM code has dimension 1040. The theorem proves that no strict `F_2`-additive outer supercode of `R` retains the target distance under this fixed blockwise encoder. Equivalently, every affine-fiber Cayley one-bit lift is either dependent or invalid.

Second, for any ordered multiset `(d_i)_{i=1}^{32768}` in any binary vector space, form all `2^30` ordered XOR pairs `(d_i+d_j)_{i,j}`. If their character code meets the target, its homogeneous dimension is at most 784; adjoining the all-one word raises this to at most 785.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Let `F` have characteristic two, `A⊂F`, `t<|A|`, `R=ev_A(F[X]_{≤t})`, and `Δ(u)=N_0(u)−N_1(u)`. If some `t`-set `S⊂A` satisfies `Σ_{a∈A\S}(∏_{s∈S}(a−s))^−1≠0`, then every strict additive supercode `D⊃R` contains a nonzero `u` with `Δ(u)≥t+1`. The proof is a `t`-point interpolation pencil. At the current parameters the explicit witness has reciprocal sum `[e1f0]≠0`, so the fixed RS–RM outer code is additively maximal.

The proof uses the identity `W_out(a)=W_seed(a)^2` and the exact 174th-moment certificate `L−1448^174>2^1825`. Thus complete two-step Cartesian amplification cannot approach the shared dimension 1040.

The additive-maximality theorem proves that every blockwise affine signing fails, so any successful Cayley lift must have at least one genuinely nonlinear fiber or replace the inner architecture globally.

proof_markdown:
## 1. Exact affine-fiber spectrum

Let `F=F_2[θ]/(P)`, where `P(θ)=θ^16+θ^5+θ^3+θ^2+1`, and let `A=span_F2{1,θ,…,θ^14}`. The shared field certificate proves that `F` has 65,536 elements. Put

`R=ev_A(F[X]_{≤64})⊂F^A`.

For `z=Σ_{i=0}^{15}z_iθ^i`, define

`Φ(z)_y=z_0+Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`,  `y∈F_2^15`.

The inner signed sum is `+2^15` for `z=0`, `−2^15` for `z=1`, and zero otherwise. The last assertion follows by pairing `y` with `y+e_i` for a nonzero linear coefficient. Therefore, writing

`Δ(u)=N_0(u)−N_1(u)`,

one has exactly

`W(Φ^A(u))=2^15Δ(u)`,

`wt(Φ^A(u))=2^14(32768−Δ(u))`.

Consequently the immutable distance is equivalent to `Δ(u)≤64` for every nonzero outer vector.

## 2. Interpolation-pencil lemma

Let `f∈F^A\R`, and suppose every vector in the coset `f+R` satisfies `Δ≤64`. Fix any 64-set `S⊂A`. Let `p_S` be the unique polynomial of degree at most 63 interpolating `f` on `S`, and put

`h_S(X)=∏_{s∈S}(X−s)`.

For each `λ∈F`, define

`u_λ=f+ev_A(p_S+λh_S)`.

Every `u_λ` lies in `f+R`, so it is neither zero nor one. At each point of `S`, all `u_λ` vanish. At each `a∈A\S`, the map `λ↦u_λ(a)` is a bijection of `F`. Hence

`Σ_{λ∈F}Δ(u_λ)=64|F|`.

Since each summand is at most 64, every summand equals 64.

For `a∉S`, set

`α_a=(f(a)+p_S(a))/h_S(a)`,

`β_a=(f(a)+p_S(a)+1)/h_S(a)=α_a+h_S(a)^−1`.

Then

`Δ(u_λ)=64+#{a:α_a=λ}−#{a:β_a=λ}`.

Equality with 64 for every `λ` says that the multisets `{α_a}` and `{β_a}` coincide. Their sums must therefore agree, forcing

`Σ_{a∈A\S}h_S(a)^−1=0`. 

Thus one explicit 64-set with nonzero reciprocal sum rules out every `f∉R`.

## 3. Explicit reciprocal-sum certificate

Represent a field element by `[w]`, where hexadecimal bit `i` is the coefficient of `θ^i`. Let

`U=span{1,θ,…,θ^5}`,

`e=[003f]=1+θ+⋯+θ^5`, `δ=[0040]=θ^6`, `u=e+δ=[007f]`,

and choose

`S=(U\{e})∪{δ}`.

Let `L_U(X)=∏_{x∈U}(X−x)`. Starting with `L_0=X`, the recurrence

`L_{i+1}=L_i^2+L_i(θ^i)L_i`,  `0≤i≤5`,

produces

`L_U(X)=[6115]X+[c6ca]X^2+[2198]X^4+[d9a4]X^8+[71ee]X^16+[2e0c]X^32+X^64`.

Put `c=[6115]=L_U'`, `c_1=[c6ca]`, `d=L_U(δ)=[e9f1]`, and

`r=Σ_{x∈U\{0}}x^−1=c_1/c=[b0cf]`.

The equality for `r` follows by comparing the first two coefficients of `L_U(X)/X`.

Since

`h_S(X)=L_U(X)(X−δ)/(X−e)`,

the omitted point `e` contributes `(cu)^−1`. For `a∈A\U`, `a≠δ`,

`h_S(a)^−1=L_U(a)^−1+u((a+δ)L_U(a))^−1`.

Let `B=L_U(A)`. Its dimension is nine and every fiber of `L_U:A→B` has 64 points. Full fibers cancel in characteristic two. The fiber over `d` has only 63 terms after deleting `δ`, so

`Σ_{a∈A\U, a≠δ}L_U(a)^−1=d^−1`.

For the second sum, the fiber over `d` contributes `r/d`. For `y∈B\{0,d}`, logarithmic differentiation of `L_U(X)+(y+d)` gives

`Σ_{L_U(z)=y+d}z^−1=c/(y+d)`.

Its aggregate contribution is

`Σ_{y∈B\{0,d}} c/[y(y+d)]=0`,

because `1/[y(y+d)]=d^−1(1/y+1/(y+d))` and translation by `d` permutes `B\{0,d}`. Therefore

`Σ_{a∈A\S}h_S(a)^−1=(cu)^−1+(1+ur)/d`.

The following exact products, all modulo `P`, finish the certificate:

`[6115][b0cf]=[c6ca]`,

`[e9f1][073e]=[0001]`,

`[6115][007f]=[5ba3]`,

`[5ba3][3c17]=[0001]`,

`[007f][b0cf]=[b576]`,

`[b577][073e]=[dde7]`,

`[3c17]+[dde7]=[e1f0]≠0`.

Thus the required reciprocal sum is nonzero.

## 4. Additive maximality and Cayley interpretation

For every `f∉R`, the preceding contradiction proves that some `u∈f+R` has integer `Δ(u)≥65`. Hence

`wt(Φ^A(u))≤2^14(32768−65)=535805952`.

If an additive space `D` strictly contains `R`, choose `f∈D\R`; then `f+R⊂D`, so `D` contains this bad vector. Therefore `R` is maximal among additive outer spaces meeting the target under `Φ^A`.

A Cayley one-bit lift assigns a bit `b(a,y)` to every existing generator. If every fiber `b(a,·)` is affine, there is a unique `f(a)∈F` with `b(a,·)=Φ(f(a))`. If `f∈R`, the new row is dependent. Otherwise the bad coset member has raw character sum

`2^15Δ(u)≥65·32768=2129920>2^21`.

Thus every affine-fiber lift is dependent or violates the target.

## 5. Complete XOR-square convolution

Let `m=32768`, let `(d_i)_{i=1}^m` be any ordered multiset in a binary vector space, and let

`H=span{d_i+d_j:1≤i,j≤m}`.

The complete ordered-pair character code has length `m^2=2^30` and dimension `k=dim H`. Put `e_i=d_i+d_1`; these vectors span `H`. For `a∈H*`, define

`W_a=Σ_i(−1)^{a(e_i)}`.

The raw signed sum of the corresponding output word is exactly

`Σ_{i,j}(−1)^{a(d_i+d_j)}=W_a^2`.

Thus the target gives `|W_a|≤1448` for every nonzero `a`, since

`1448^2=2096704<2^21<2099601=1449^2`.

Take `r=87`. Let `Z` count ordered 174-tuples of seed indices whose `e`-values XOR to zero. Fourier orthogonality gives

`2^k Z=Σ_{a∈H*}W_a^174≤m^174+(2^k−1)1448^174`.

Tuples formed by choosing 87 distinct indices and using each exactly twice give

`Z≥L=binom(m,87)174!/2^87`.

Hence

`2^k(L−1448^174)<m^174`.

It remains only to certify the denominator. Write

`L=[∏_{j=0}^{86}(32768−j)][∏_{j=88}^{174}j]/2^87`.

The elementary inequality `∏(1−x_j)≥1−Σx_j` gives

`∏_{j=0}^{86}(32768−j)> (7/8)2^1305`,

because `Σ_{j=0}^{86}j=3741` and `1−3741/32768>7/8`. Direct exact integer multiplication gives

`7∏_{j=88}^{174}j>5·2^610`.

Therefore `L>5·2^1825`. Also `1448^174=(1448^2)^87<2^1827=4·2^1825`, so

`L−1448^174>2^1825`.

Since `m^174=(2^15)^174=2^2610`, it follows that

`2^k<2^785`,

and hence `k≤784`.

Every square-convolution word has nonnegative raw signed sum. Consequently adjoining the all-one word preserves the target by complementing these words and adds at most one dimension. Even this affine closure has dimension at most 785.

proof_steps.proof: Character orthogonality gives inner signed sums `+2^15`, `−2^15`, and zero at symbols `0`, `1`, and all other symbols. Summing the blocks gives the displayed exact weight formula.

Interpolate a proposed new direction on 64 points and vary the coefficient of their vanishing polynomial. Averaging `Δ` over all field coefficients forces equality in every member of the pencil; equality of the zero- and one-parameter multisets then forces the reciprocal sum to vanish.
proof_steps.statement: If every word in a coset `f+R`, `f∉R`, satisfies `Δ≤64`, then every 64-set `S⊂A` has `Σ_{a∉S}h_S(a)^−1=0`.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed linearized polynomial, its 64-point fibers, logarithmic derivative identity, and exact hexadecimal field products give reciprocal sum `[e1f0]`.
proof_steps.statement: The fixed set `S=(span{1,…,θ^5}\{1+⋯+θ^5})∪{θ^6}` has nonzero reciprocal sum.

proof_steps.proof: For every `f∉R`, the nonzero certificate contradicts the assumption that all of `f+R` has `Δ≤64`; integrality supplies a member with `Δ≥65`. Any strict additive supercode contains such a coset.
proof_steps.statement: No strict additive outer supercode of `R` meets the target under the fixed affine inner encoder.

proof_steps.proof: Every affine fiber is uniquely `Φ(f(a))`. A dependent `f` lies in `R`; otherwise additive maximality gives a character sum at least `65·2^15>2^21`.
proof_steps.statement: Every affine-fiber Cayley one-bit lift is dependent or violates the spectral threshold.

proof_steps.proof: Translate the seeds by `d_1`. The output character sum factors into the product of two identical seed sums.
proof_steps.statement: For complete ordered XOR-square convolution, every output character sum is `W_a^2`.

proof_steps.proof: Fourier orthogonality counts zero-XOR 174-tuples. Restricting to 87 distinct indices each repeated twice gives `Z≥binom(32768,87)174!/2^87`.
proof_steps.statement: The complete convolution satisfies the stated 174th-moment inequality.

proof_steps.proof: The exact dyadic certificate gives `L−1448^174>2^1825`, while the numerator is `2^2610`. Thus `2^k<2^785`.
proof_steps.statement: Every target-meeting complete square convolution has homogeneous dimension at most 784 and all-one-extended dimension at most 785.

research_direction: Spectral amplification via Cayley lifts, affine-fiber extensions, and complete XOR convolution
theorem_statement: In the explicit `F_{2^16}` RS–RM architecture, the degree-at-most-64 outer evaluation space `R` is maximal among `F_2`-additive outer spaces whose blockwise affine descent has minimum distance at least 535,822,336. More sharply, every `f∉R` has `u∈f+R` with `N_0(u)−N_1(u)≥65`, so the corresponding binary word has weight at most 535,805,952. Separately, every complete ordered XOR-square convolution of 32,768 seeds meeting the target has homogeneous dimension at most 784, or at most 785 after adjoining the all-one word.
title: Additive maximality of affine-fiber Cayley lifts and a k≤784 convolution ceiling
